title: Assignment 02 · Introduction to remedies
summary: Introduction to remedies. Assigned readings and principal cases for this class.
notes:
Sullivan v. O’Connor: A patient recovered for expenses, worsened appearance, and an additional operation after a promised cosmetic result failed. The parties’ appellate waivers limited the court’s need to choose between expectation and reliance measures.

United States Naval Institute v. Charter Communications, Inc.: Contract damages compensated the publisher’s lost hardcover profits; the licensee’s separate profits were not recoverable merely because its early paperback sales breached the agreement.

Morris v. Sparrow: A horse that the claimant had personally trained had sufficiently distinctive value to justify delivery of that horse rather than an award of its market price.

White v. Benkowski: Actual inconvenience supported modest compensatory damages for deliberate water interruptions, but malice alone did not support punitive damages on the contract claim presented.
